clue.text: Party food shown as pecan nuts

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters of the words before it go wild and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A host serves pecans as nibbles at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' looks like part of the food, but it is the anagram signal: AS PECAN rearranged gives the answer; 'shown' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: These small savoury bites on bread or pastry are classic finger food at a drinks party.

clue.text: Young scout is hanging around street artists

parts.note: a Cub is a junior member of the Scout movement

indicators.note: the word is hangs around the street abbreviation, enclosing it

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A young scout loiters on the street where painters work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'street' looks like where the scout hangs about, but it gives its abbreviation, which 'hanging around' puts inside 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Picasso and Braque led this early twentieth-century school of painters, so its members are a kind of artist.

clue.text: What starts a procession is a "pee"!

definitions.meaning: the first in line, at the head of a parade
childish euphemism for urinating, as opposed to number two

explanation.surface: A mock-solemn remark that the leader of a parade is a toilet break.
explanation.definitionFit: The leader of a parade is the first in order; nursery talk calls a wee by the same numeral.

clue.text: Tart up for prince and one politician

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
MP, Member of Parliament, is a British politician

explanation.surface: Someone smartens up ready to meet royalty and a member of Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: To tart up is to dress or groom oneself fussily, the same as preening.

clue.text: Move suddenly close to bus — crash!

definitions.note: the clue gives the present tense, though the answer is past tense

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so take the final letter of bus

parts.note: prang is British slang for a minor crash, especially of a car

explanation.surface: Something lurched just before a bus crashed.
explanation.walkthrough: PRANG is informal British English for a crash or bump in a vehicle. The definition should read 'Moved suddenly' to match the past tense; bloggers flagged the slip.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of spring, which means to jump or leap abruptly.

clue.text: Type of award fixed in memory

indicators.note: the word for fixed is placed in the word for memory

parts.note: learning by rote means by memory
set means fixed, as in set in stone

explanation.surface: A certain prize is lodged permanently in someone's mind.
explanation.definitionFit: A ribbon badge given as a prize at shows, so it is one kind of award.

clue.text: Swedes, say,cheer on group

parts.note: to root for a team is to cheer it on
a crop of things is a group of them appearing together, like a crop of new players

explanation.surface: Scandinavians are cheering on a band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swedes' looks like people from Sweden, but here it is the vegetable (swede is the British name for rutabaga).
explanation.definitionFit: Swedes are turnip-like vegetables grown for their edible underground part, examples of this category.

clue.text: Romanians reformed the republic

indicators.note: reformed means formed again, so the letters of Romanians are rearranged

explanation.surface: Romanians remodelled their republic.
explanation.walkthrough: The republic meant is not Romania but the tiny state inside Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny state enclosed by Italy, it is one of the world's oldest republics.

clue.text: G-string air provided by person with lisp

indicators.note: a lisper says th where s is meant, so the s sound in the tune word becomes th

parts.note: an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: A tune about skimpy underwear is sung by someone who lisps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'G-string' may suggest a violin string, matching 'air', but it is underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are skimpy pieces of underwear or swimwear with a narrow strip at the back.

clue.text: Rolls following first pair of English volunteers?

indicators.note: the rolls word comes after the two letters
take the first two letters of English

parts.note: rolls are lists of names, as in the electoral roll

explanation.surface: Rolls-Royce cars follow English volunteers, a question asks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolls' looks like the car; here it means registers of names.
explanation.definitionFit: To sign up for the forces is to offer oneself, so enlists means volunteers.

clue.text: Rotten landing is rougher

parts.note: bum is slang for of poor quality, as in a bum deal
a pier is a landing stage for boats

explanation.surface: An aircraft's bad landing is a rough one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'landing' suggests an aircraft touching down; it is a jetty.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of bumpy: a more uneven ride is rougher.

clue.text: Have girl holding ring, an embarrassing error

parts.note: to own something is to have it

indicators.note: the girl word holds the ring letter inside it

parts.note: gal is an informal word for girl
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A man with a girlfriend holding a ring makes a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: In football, scoring in your own net is the classic embarrassing blunder.

clue.text: Wholesale new arrangements for a daily?

definitions.meaning: a daily is a British cleaning lady; her work changes involve brushing floors

explanation.surface: Big reorganisations are planned for a cleaner.
explanation.walkthrough: A daily is British slang for a cleaner who comes in each day, not a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Wholesale reforms are far-reaching; a cleaner's duties alter by sweeping floors.

clue.text: Issue about marijuana? Absolutely

indicators.note: the issue word goes about, surrounding, the marijuana word

parts.note: issue means offspring, so a son
pot is slang for marijuana

explanation.surface: A dispute over cannabis is settled firmly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' looks like a problem; here it means a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot on is British slang for exactly right, so it serves as an emphatic yes.

clue.text: In risky situation with a cracking future?

definitions.meaning: standing where the frozen surface may soon break

explanation.surface: Someone in peril may soon go through the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in danger; literally, a skater over fragile frozen water may hear it break.

clue.text: Feeling unwell, long to enter area of northern Scotland

indicators.note: the long word goes into the area word

parts.note: Ross, as in Ross and Cromarty, is a region of the Scottish Highlands
to pine is to long for

explanation.surface: Someone sick longs to get into the Highlands.
explanation.walkthrough: Ross is part of the Scottish Highlands; ropey is British slang for unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Ropey is British slang for poorly, so this noun is the state of being off-colour.

clue.text: Admit it's a complaint

parts.note: to admit someone is to let them enter
it's expanded is it is

explanation.surface: Confess that it is a grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' looks like a grievance; here it is an ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflammation of the intestines is a medical disorder, and complaint means an illness.

clue.text: Heard popular drinks for those with an advantage

indicators.note: heard signals that the words are judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: popular is in, and drinks are ciders

explanation.surface: Word is that trendy drinks benefit the privileged.
explanation.definitionFit: People on the inside of an organisation have privileged knowledge.

clue.text: Manifest single part of harmonic series

parts.note: overt means open and plain to see
one is a single unit

explanation.surface: One clear component of a musical set is shown.
explanation.definitionFit: A higher tone sounding above the fundamental belongs to the harmonic series in acoustics.

clue.text: Source for supplying cooker direct

parts.note: a cooker is a cooking apple, so this is where such fruit is grown and supplied straight from the tree

explanation.surface: A place where you can buy a kitchen stove straight from the maker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooker' looks like a kitchen stove, but in Britain it also means a cooking apple.
explanation.definitionFit: Apple trees are grown in a plot of fruit trees, the direct source of cooking apples.

clue.text: Pitcher perhaps showing courage

definitions.meaning: a jug or flask for holding liquid
British slang for nerve, as in losing your nerve

explanation.surface: A baseball pitcher is displaying nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitcher is a vessel for liquid; British slang uses the same word for nerve or guts.

clue.text: Perhaps I part with kettle

definitions.meaning: I is the chemical symbol for iodine
the heating coil inside an electric kettle

explanation.surface: Someone muses on parting with their kettle.
explanation.definitionFit: Iodine is a chemical substance in the periodic table, and a heating coil goes by the same word.

clue.text: Live within, leaving hospital shortly

indicators.note: the hospital letter leaves, so it is removed

parts.note: to inhabit a place is to live within it
H is the hospital sign

explanation.surface: Someone resides in a ward, soon to be discharged.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean soon, after a short time.

clue.text: Crash training is what looks like leading to conflict

definitions.text: what looks like leading to conflict

parts.note: a collision is a crash
a course is a programme of training

explanation.surface: An instruction programme on car crashes seems headed for trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things on this path are heading for impact, so the idiom means headed for confrontation.

clue.text: Winds reel up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a spool is a reel for thread or film

explanation.surface: Someone coils up a reel of thread.
explanation.definitionFit: To wind a rope is to coil it round in circles.

clue.text: Something round for each end of sauna could be soap

parts.note: O is round in shape
per means for each, as in per person

indicators.note: take the last letter of sauna

explanation.surface: Something circular for each sauna could be a bar of soap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soap' looks like a washing bar in the sauna; it is soap opera, a TV serial.
explanation.definitionFit: A soap opera is a type of drama, so soap names one example of this kind.

clue.text: Destroy short book inspired by a long book

indicators.note: inspired means breathed in, so the short book goes inside the long book

parts.note: a tome is a large heavy volume
Is is the abbreviation for the Book of Isaiah

explanation.surface: A short work drew inspiration from a long work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inspired by' looks like a matter of influence; read literally it means breathed in, so one book goes inside the other. Is. is the Bible's abbreviation for Isaiah.
explanation.definitionFit: To reduce something to tiny particles is to destroy it.

clue.text: Expel gas from second-grade, broken heater

parts.note: B is the second grade after A

indicators.note: broken means the letters of heater are smashed and reformed

explanation.surface: Gas escapes from an inferior, faulty heater.
explanation.definitionFit: Breathing involves exhaling air, which is a gas.

clue.text: Vagrants seen in brief I ignored

definitions.note: plural noun, matching the plural answer

indicators.note: the letter I is ignored, so it is left out of the word for the brief

parts.note: a barrister's brief is a bundle of case papers, a set of dossiers

explanation.surface: Homeless people turn up in a legal case that took no notice of me.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads 'brief' where the word needed is plural; the blog suggests 'briefs' was meant, but a brief can be taken as a collection of files. 'seen in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Dosser is British slang for a homeless person who sleeps rough or in cheap lodgings.

clue.text: What's all this PC stuff? I've had enough!

definitions.meaning: PC stuff is computing, abbreviated IT; asked what it is, one replies it is IT

explanation.surface: An exasperated person gives up on computer jargon.
explanation.walkthrough: IT is information technology, the stuff of PCs.
explanation.definitionFit: The first reading identifies computing as the topic; the second is an idiom for reaching one's limit.
